cleaner.title: Deep cleanup
cleaner.recoverable: Up to {{size}} can be reclaimed. Review what each item does before cleaning.
cleaner.preserved: Never touched: your documents, passwords, bookmarks, extensions, browser settings and installed programs.
cleaner.notElevatedWin: RePID is not running as administrator, so system-level items (Windows temp, update cache) will be skipped.
cleaner.notElevatedUnix: System-level items will ask for your password once when you clean.

unavailable.not-found: Nothing to clean here right now.
unavailable.needs-full-disk-access: macOS blocks access. Grant RePID "Full Disk Access" in System Settings → Privacy & Security, then scan again.
unavailable.unsupported: Not available on this operating system.

cleaner.blockedBy: {{names}} is open. It must close to clean this — you will be asked first.
cleaner.needsAdminNote: Will be skipped without administrator rights.

status.partial: Partly cleaned · {{size}} freed · {{skipped}} in use or protected
status.skipped-running: Skipped: the app was still open

user-temp.title: Temporary files & user caches
user-temp.effect: Deletes temporary files, crash reports and thumbnail/shader caches. Apps recreate them when needed; the first launch of some games or apps may be a little slower. Files currently in use are skipped.

system-temp.title: System temporary files
system-temp.effect: Deletes system-wide temporary files and old error reports. Your documents are not affected; files in use are skipped. Needs administrator rights.

update-cache.title: Update download cache
update-cache.effect: Deletes already-downloaded update installers. Installed updates are NOT removed; if an update is still pending, the system will download it again.

recycle-bin.title: Recycle Bin / Trash
recycle-bin.effect: PERMANENTLY deletes everything in the recycle bin. This cannot be undone and the files cannot be recovered.

dns-cache.title: DNS cache
dns-cache.effect: Flushes cached domain-name lookups. Helps when a site fails to load after a network change. No downside: the next visits simply resolve names again.

dev-caches.title: Package manager caches (npm, Yarn, pip)
dev-caches.effect: Deletes downloaded package caches. Your projects are untouched, but the next install will download packages again (slower and needs internet).

browser-cache.title: Cache
browser-cache.effect: Deletes images, scripts and files saved from websites. Pages load a little slower the first time. You stay signed in and passwords are kept.

browser-history.title: Browsing history
browser-history.effect: Deletes visited pages, address-bar suggestions, most-visited tiles and the tabs saved for "restore session". Cannot be undone. Bookmarks and passwords are kept.

browser-cookies.title: Cookies & sign-ins
browser-cookies.effect: Signs you out of EVERY website (email, social networks, banking) and erases site preferences. You will need to sign in again and may have to repeat two-step verification.

app-caches.title: App caches
app-caches.effect: Clears the cache of apps such as Discord, Slack, VS Code, Postman or Notion (images, compiled code and GPU cache). They rebuild automatically; the first launch is a bit slower. Your sessions, messages and settings are untouched. Files in use are skipped.

crash-dumps.title: Crash memory dumps
crash-dumps.effect: Files Windows saves after a blue screen or a hang (MEMORY.DMP, Minidump). They only help diagnose crashes that already happened and can take several GB.

windows-old.title: Previous Windows installation and update leftovers
windows-old.effect: Uses Windows' own cleanup tool to delete Windows.old, temporary setup files and components of updates already applied. Afterwards you can no longer go back to the previous Windows version or uninstall those updates. It can take several minutes.

confirm.title: Review before cleaning
confirm.body: This is exactly what will happen:
confirm.sensitiveTitle: These items are irreversible or will sign you out:
confirm.sensitiveAck: I understand the consequences and want to continue.
confirm.closeBlockingHint: Unsaved work in those windows (open forms, downloads in progress) will be lost. If unchecked, their items are skipped.

toast.skippedRunning_one: {{count}} item skipped because its app was open.
toast.skippedRunning_other: {{count}} items skipped because their apps were open.
toast.partial_one: {{count}} item was partly cleaned (files in use).
toast.partial_other: {{count}} items were partly cleaned (files in use).

startup.title: Startup programs
startup.scanning: Checking what opens when the computer starts…
startup.summary: {{enabled}} open on their own at sign-in · {{mem}} in use right now
startup.safeNote: Disabling never uninstalls or deletes anything: the program just stops opening automatically at sign-in. You can turn it back on here any time.
startup.nextBoot: Takes effect at your next sign-in. Apps that are already open stay open.
startup.notElevatedWin: Some programs are registered for every user of this computer; changing them requires administrator rights.
startup.unsupported: Startup management is not available on this platform.
startup.whatHappens: What happens if you disable it:
startup.suggestedHint: Rarely needed at startup and safe to disable.
startup.lockedHint: Operating-system component or locked by policy: RePID will not disable it.
startup.adminHint: Registered for all users: requires administrator rights.
startup.impactHint: Measured now from what it uses while open.

effect.updater: It will check for updates when you open the program instead of sitting in the background from boot.
effect.browser: The browser (or web app) won't preload at sign-in; the first time you open it may take a couple of seconds longer.
effect.communication: You won't get messages or calls from this app until you open it yourself.
effect.media: The app won't open on its own. Your music, library and settings stay intact.
effect.gaming: The launcher won't open on its own. Your games stay installed; downloads and updates start when you open it.
effect.cloud: Your files stop syncing until you open the app: anything you change meanwhile won't be backed up to the cloud.
effect.security: It may stop alerting you or protecting in real time whatever this product watches. Only do this if you know you don't need it.
effect.hardware: Hardware features that rely on this utility may stop working: special keys, audio controls, lighting, advanced touchpad, or camera and microphone effects.
effect.development: Developer tools (containers, local servers) won't be ready until you open them.
effect.system: It is part of the operating system and stays enabled.
effect.generic: The program won't open automatically; you can open it yourself whenever you need it.

confirm.title: Disable at startup
confirm.body: These programs will stop opening automatically at sign-in. Nothing is uninstalled or deleted.
confirm.cautionAck: I understand what will happen and want to disable them anyway.

history.title: Changes made by RePID
history.body_one: RePID disabled {{count}} program. You can put it back exactly as it was in one click.
history.body_other: RePID disabled {{count}} programs. You can put everything back exactly as it was in one click.

toast.disabled_one: {{name}} will no longer open at sign-in
toast.disabled_other: {{count}} programs will no longer open at sign-in
toast.enabled_other: {{count}} programs will open at sign-in again
toast.protected_one: {{count}} is protected and was left alone.
toast.protected_other: {{count}} are protected and were left alone.

boost.title: Performance mode
boost.inactive: Off · pick a profile to prioritize what you're doing
boost.safeNote: No app is closed and nothing is deleted. The selected apps keep working; they just yield CPU to what you're using. Everything goes back to normal when you press “Restore all”, close RePID, or restart the app.

gaming.title: Gaming
gaming.desc: Priority to your game. Browsers, sync and updaters yield CPU. Voice chat, overlays and launchers are left alone.

work.title: Focus
work.desc: Game launchers and background processes yield CPU to your work apps.

creative.title: Render / build
creative.desc: Everything non-essential yields CPU to your editor, renderer or build.

custom.title: Custom
custom.desc: You choose which apps to adjust; nothing is pre-selected.

focus.label: Priority app
focus.hint: Gets above-normal priority. “High” and “Realtime” are never used: they can freeze keyboard and audio.
focus.unsupported: On macOS and Linux raising priority requires root; RePID only lowers the other apps.

boost.listHint: Pre-selected by the profile. You can change the selection.
boost.ecoEffect: It keeps working normally; when the computer is busy it waits its turn and may respond a little slower while the mode is on.
boost.ecoQosNote: On Windows 11 it also turns on “Efficiency mode” (the green leaf in Task Manager).
boost.protectedCount_one: {{count}} system, service or security app is left alone.
boost.protectedCount_other: {{count}} system, service and security apps are left alone.
boost.empty: No background app is using a meaningful amount of resources right now.
boost.notRunning: Closed · will be adjusted if you open it again
boost.restorePending: Some priorities could not be restored because the password prompt was cancelled. They return to normal when those apps restart.
boost.detailHint: Lowers its priority without closing it. Restored when you turn it off or close RePID.
boost.detailBlocked: System apps, services, security software and apps marked caution keep their priority.

toast.stopped: All restored: apps are back to their original priority

uninstall.title: Smart uninstaller
uninstall.safeNote: The app's own uninstaller runs first; then RePID looks for what it left behind: folders, caches, registry keys, shortcuts and startup entries. Files go to the Recycle Bin and keys are backed up before deletion, so everything can be recovered.
uninstall.unsupported: The uninstaller is not available on this platform.
uninstall.linuxNote: On Linux RePID manages Flatpak apps. System packages (apt, dnf, pacman) are removed with your distribution's package manager.
uninstall.notElevated: Apps installed for all users need administrator rights to be uninstalled and cleaned up.

kindHint.runtime: Other apps may need this component; removing it can stop them from opening.
kindHint.driver: It's a driver or hardware utility: sound, display, printer or other devices may stop working.
kindHint.security: It's security software: your computer may be unprotected until you install another one.
kindHint.system: It's part of the operating system.

lockedHint.runtime: Shared component other apps rely on (such as .NET, Visual C++ or WebView2): RePID won't uninstall it.
lockedHint.system: Operating-system component: RePID won't uninstall it.

reason.name-match: Folder or key with the app's exact name
reason.vendor-dir: Inside the publisher's folder, with the app's name
reason.points-to-app: Opens a file of the app
reason.orphan: Belongs to no installed app, service, driver, process, startup entry or shortcut
reason.broken-target: Points to a program that no longer exists
reason.broken-entry: Listed in “Installed apps”, but its uninstaller and folder are gone

status.still-installed: {{name}} is still installed: the uninstaller seems to have been cancelled or didn't finish. RePID doesn't look for leftovers of an installed app so it won't break it.
status.uninstaller-failed: {{name}}'s uninstaller ended with an error. Nothing else was touched.
status.protected: {{name}} is protected and was not uninstalled.
status.cancelled: Uninstalling {{name}} was cancelled. Nothing was touched.

wizard.title: Uninstall {{name}}

body.win32: {{name}}'s official uninstaller will open. Complete its steps; when it finishes, RePID will look for what it left behind.
body.msi: Windows Installer will uninstall {{name}}. When it finishes, RePID will look for what it left behind.
body.store: {{name}} will be removed the same way Windows Settings does it. Then RePID checks for leftover data.
body.mac-app: {{name}} will be moved to the Trash. Then RePID looks for its preferences, caches and data in your Library.
body.flatpak: Flatpak will uninstall {{name}}. Then RePID looks for leftover data.

wizard.point1: Nothing is deleted without your review: you'll see every leftover before removing it.
wizard.point2: Only leftovers that clearly belong to this app are ticked, never other apps' folders.
wizard.point3: Files go to the Recycle Bin and registry keys are backed up: everything can be recovered.
wizard.closeRunning_one: Close {{count}} open process of the app before uninstalling
wizard.closeRunning_other: Close {{count}} open processes of the app before uninstalling
wizard.quietHint: No uninstaller windows or questions. Uses the vendor's default options.
wizard.ack: I understand what will happen and want to continue.
wizard.missingTitle: This app's uninstaller no longer exists
wizard.missingBody: {{name}}'s registered uninstaller is no longer on disk, so it can't run. RePID can look for what's left of the app (including its entry in “Installed apps”) so you can remove it.
wizard.runningHint: If an uninstaller window opened, complete its steps. RePID continues as soon as it finishes.
wizard.leftoversBody_one: Found {{count}} leftover ({{size}}). Ticked items clearly belong to the app; review the rest before including it.
wizard.leftoversBody_other: Found {{count}} leftovers ({{size}}). Ticked items clearly belong to the app; review the rest before including them.
wizard.recoverable: Files and folders go to the Recycle Bin; registry keys and tasks are backed up before deletion.
wizard.doneAdmin_one: {{count}} leftover needs administrator rights; restart RePID as administrator to remove it.
wizard.doneAdmin_other: {{count}} leftovers need administrator rights; restart RePID as administrator to remove them.
wizard.doneFailed_one: {{count}} leftover could not be removed (it may be in use).
wizard.doneFailed_other: {{count}} leftovers could not be removed (they may be in use).
wizard.backupNote: To recover a registry key, open the backups and double-click its .reg file.

orphans.title: Leftovers of uninstalled apps
orphans.scanning: Looking for what apps you no longer have left behind…
orphans.scanningHint: RePID checks every folder against your installed apps, services, drivers, processes, startup entries and shortcuts. It can take a minute.
orphans.body_one: Found {{count}} leftover ({{size}}) of apps that are no longer installed.
orphans.body_other: Found {{count}} leftovers ({{size}}) of apps that are no longer installed.
orphans.how: Only things no app, service or driver uses and that haven't changed in 60+ days are shown. Broken shortcuts and entries and program-free folders unused for months are ticked; review the rest (they may be game saves or portable tools). Everything goes to the Recycle Bin or is backed up.
orphans.none: All clean! No leftovers of uninstalled apps.
orphans.review: contains programs or saved games, review it

disk.title: What is filling your disk?
disk.intro: Analyze a folder or drive and see on a map what takes space, your biggest files and duplicates.
disk.safeNote: Everything you delete goes to the Recycle Bin. Windows, installed programs, app data and tool folders (.git, node_modules, .gradle…) are shown but never offered for deletion.
disk.hashing: Comparing file contents to find identical copies…
disk.truncated: The analysis stopped early (cancelled or too many files): sizes may be lower than the real ones.
disk.oldOnly: Only files not modified for more than a year
disk.noLarge: No files of 100 MB or more here.
disk.dupIntro: RePID looks for files with exactly the same content (not just the same name): first by size, then by comparing their SHA-256 fingerprint. Libraries and program files are never included.
disk.dupTruncated: Up to 40 GB were compared: the groups that free the most space come first.
disk.noDuplicates: No duplicate files of 1 MB or more were found.

confirm.title: Move to the Recycle Bin?
confirm.body_one: {{count}} file ({{size}}) will be moved to the Recycle Bin.
confirm.body_other: {{count}} files ({{size}}) will be moved to the Recycle Bin.
confirm.recycle: You can restore them from the Recycle Bin. The space is really freed when you empty it. RePID always keeps at least one copy of every duplicate.

toast.done_other: {{count}} files moved to the Recycle Bin ({{size}})

toast.refused_other: {{count}} were skipped because they changed since the analysis or were the last copy.

toast.failed_other: {{count}} could not be moved (in use or no permission).

automation.title: RePID working for you
automation.intro: Turn on what you want RePID to do by itself: speed up your games, clean what is safe and warn you before problems happen.
automation.boostingNow: Performance mode turned on automatically for {{name}}.
automation.onlyWhileOpen: All of this works while RePID is open. Turn on "Keep running in the background" so it works even after you close the window.

boost.title: Automatic performance mode
boost.body: When you open a game or an app from your list, RePID prioritizes it and calms what runs in the background. It turns off by itself when you close it.
boost.games: Detect games (Steam, Epic, GOG, Xbox, EA, Ubisoft, Riot, Battle.net)

clean.title: Scheduled cleanup
clean.body: Cleans only what is marked safe (temporary files, caches). Never history, passwords or anything an open app is using, and never while you play.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.body: System notifications when something needs your attention.
alerts.memory: An app keeps growing in memory (possible leak)

background.title: Keep running in the background

background.tray: When the window closes, stay in the tray

log.boost-off: {{name}} closed: performance mode off and priorities restored

updates.title: Update your apps
updates.intro: Looks for new versions of your installed programs.

note.darwin: Uses Homebrew (formulae and casks installed with brew).
note.linux: Uses Flatpak for apps installed with Flatpak.

missing.win32: winget was not found. Install "App Installer" from the Microsoft Store to use this feature.
missing.linux: Flatpak was not found on this system.

updates.unsupported: This feature is not available on this system.
updates.applyingHint: It can take a few minutes per app. Keep RePID open.
updates.majorHint: Major version jump (for example 11 → 13): it may change how the app works or its data format. Review before updating; that is why it is not selected.

health.title: Computer health
health.intro: Your drives, battery, temperatures and space, explained simply.
health.needsAdmin: Drive wear, temperature and errors can only be read as administrator.
health.noCpuTemp: Your computer does not expose the processor temperature without the manufacturer's tools.

findings.allGood: All good: no health problems found.

findings.driveWarning: Drive {{name}} reports warnings. A backup is a good idea.

findings.driveWear: SSD {{name}} has used {{pct}}% of its lifespan.

findings.batteryAged: The battery holds {{pct}}% of its original capacity: it lasts less than when it was new.
findings.cpuHot: The processor is at {{temp}} °C: clean the dust or check the ventilation.
findings.gpuHot: The graphics card is at {{temp}} °C: check the ventilation.

network.summary_one: {{count}} app connected to the internet now
network.summary_other: {{count}} apps connected to the internet now

network.needsAdmin: To block an app's internet access, RePID needs administrator rights.
network.blockedIdle: Programs blocked by RePID (not open now)
network.empty: No app has open connections right now.

status.blocked: {{name}} can no longer connect to the internet
status.not-found: The app is no longer open
status.unsupported: Blocking is only available on Windows
status.failed: Could not change the firewall rule

services.title: Services that start with Windows
services.summary: {{count}} services reviewed · {{rec}} suggested to set to manual
services.safeNote: "Manual" means the service no longer starts with Windows, but it starts by itself when something needs it. RePID never disables or stops services, and never shows drivers, audio, network or security.
services.unsupported: Services are only managed on Windows. On macOS and Linux use Startup.
services.needsAdmin: Changing services requires running RePID as administrator.
services.nextBoot: The effect shows from the next restart.

catalog.telemetry: Sends usage and diagnostic data to Microsoft. On manual, Windows works the same.
catalog.maps: Downloads offline maps for the Maps app. If you do not use it, you will not notice.
catalog.retailDemo: Store demo mode. Not used on personal computers.
catalog.mediaSharing: Shares your Windows Media Player library on the local network. Starts if you use it.
catalog.fax: Sending faxes. Starts by itself if you ever send one.
catalog.linkTracking: Tracks files moved between computers on a company network. At home you will not notice.
catalog.search: Indexes files for instant search. On manual, searching in Explorer and Start will be slower.
catalog.sysmain: Preloads your most used apps into memory. Helps on slow drives (HDD); on SSDs the effect is smaller.
catalog.printing: Print queue. If you have a printer, printing keeps working but the first job takes a bit longer.
catalog.updater: Checks for updates for this app. On manual, the app still updates when you open it or through its scheduled task.
catalog.telemetryApp: Collects the vendor's analytics or diagnostics. The app works the same without it at startup.
catalog.remote: Lets others connect to this computer remotely. On manual, nobody can connect until you open the app.
catalog.database: Local database. On manual it does not start with Windows: start the database (or the app that uses it) when you need it.
catalog.license: Validates a program's license. If that program does not start afterwards, set it back to automatic.
catalog.thirdParty: Another vendor's service. It may be needed by their program: change it only if you know what it does.

confirm.title: Set these services to manual?
